cards.front: Recall a key point about Power Supplies & Regulation
cards.back: A power supply converts AC mains to a stable DC voltage through transformer, rectifier, smoothing and regulation stages.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Power Supplies & Regulation
cards.back: A step-down transformer reduces the AC mains voltage to a lower AC voltage suitable for the circuit.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Power Supplies & Regulation
cards.back: Half-wave rectification uses a single diode and only rectifies one half of the AC cycle, giving 50% efficiency.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Power Supplies & Regulation
cards.back: Full-wave rectification using a bridge rectifier uses four diodes and rectifies both halves of the AC cycle.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Power Supplies & Regulation
cards.back: The output of a rectifier is pulsating DC; a smoothing capacitor converts this to a more constant DC level.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Power Supplies & Regulation
cards.back: Ripple voltage is the residual AC variation on the DC output; larger capacitance reduces ripple for a given load current.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Power Supplies & Regulation
cards.back: Ripple voltage formula: V_ripple ≈ I_load / (f × C), where f is the ripple frequency (100 Hz for full-wave on 50 Hz mains).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Power Supplies & Regulation
cards.back: A Zener diode operates in reverse breakdown to provide a stable reference voltage; it is the simplest form of voltage regulator.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Power Supplies & Regulation
cards.back: A Zener regulator circuit uses a series resistor to limit current: R_s = (V_in − V_Z) / (I_Z + I_load).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Power Supplies & Regulation
cards.back: A three-terminal voltage regulator (e.g. 7805 for 5 V, 7812 for 12 V) provides a fixed, stable output with built-in protection.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Power Supplies & Regulation
cards.back: Linear regulators dissipate excess voltage as heat; efficiency is V_out / V_in, so they run hot when the difference is large.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Power Supplies & Regulation
cards.back: Switch-mode power supplies (SMPS) use high-frequency switching for higher efficiency and smaller size than linear regulators.

cards.front: What should you know about gcse electronics exam tips — power supplies & regulation?
cards.back: 1. For Power Supplies & Regulation questions, use correct electronic symbols and terminology 2. Always show your working in calculations, including units at each step 3. When analysing circuits, state which law or rule you are applying first 4. For evaluation questions on Power Supplies & Regulation, compare component choices and consider cost, reliability and tolerance 5. Draw circuit diagrams neatly with conventional symbols
